title: Babel
summary: Genesis 11:1-9 narrates a community in Shinar building a city and tower to make a name and avoid dispersion, followed by YHWH's confusion of speech and scattering of the builders.
historical_context: The episode belongs to Genesis's primeval history and is geographically associated with Shinar/Babylonia. Its narrative setting, composition, and relationship to Mesopotamian urban monuments are distinct historical questions.
ancient_near_east_context: Mesopotamian cities built monumental temple towers, but Genesis does not name a specific excavated ziggurat. The narrative's city, tower, bricks, bitumen, and name-making provide bounded cultural points of comparison.
hebraic_worldview: Genesis portrays human urban coordination and technological ability as real goods vulnerable to self-exalting use; YHWH frustrates the attempt to resist dispersion and secure a name autonomously.
literary_context: Babel follows the table of nations in Genesis 10 and precedes the genealogy and call of Abram in Genesis 11:10-12:3. The builders' desire to make a name contrasts with God's promise to make Abram's name great.
covenantal_significance: The scattering at Babel forms the immediate narrative backdrop to God's call of Abram and promise that all families of the earth will be blessed through him.
canonical_role: Babel closes Genesis's primeval dispersal sequence and immediately precedes the genealogy and call through which blessing is promised to all families of the earth.

related_objects.notes: Babel is associated with Shinar and Babylonian urban imagery.
The call and blessing promise follow the scattering narrative.

scripture_references.notes: The table of nations frames the dispersal of peoples.
The genealogy moves from Shem toward Abram.
God promises Abram a great name and blessing for all families.

interpretive_notes.note: The text describes a tower with its top in the heavens, an idiom of monumental height or ambition; it does not say the builders expected to climb into God's dwelling.
Ziggurats provide a cultural analogy for monumental towers in Babylonia, but identifying the narrative with one excavated structure goes beyond the evidence.

common_questions: Why do the builders want to make a name and avoid dispersion?
How does Babel connect Genesis 10 with the call of Abram?
What is the relevance of Mesopotamian ziggurats?
Does Genesis identify the tower with a specific excavated monument?
